confirmed.divergence_sequence:
Node NAS and node PI both hold the same committed vertex sequence.

T0: Some block H changes the validator set. Reachable two ways with zero user transactions: (a) executor::execute_one_slash prunes the offender from BOTH `sys:validators` (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2489) and `sys:validator_set:v1` (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2513), and that runs from `apply_slash_evidence`, which BOTH paths invoke; (b) a stake change through append_validator_upsert / append_validator_stake_resync.

T1: NAS BUILDS H locally. The commit loop persists the block and then calls `self.invalidate_validators_cache()` at dag.rs:1279 — the ONLY production call site of that method (`grep -rn invalidate_validators_cache consensus core sync da governance` returns dag.rs:365 = definition, dag.rs:1279 = this call, and tests). NAS's next read of `get_validator_set_with_stake()` is therefore FRESH: 3 validators (or the new stake).

T2: PI IMPORTS the same H through ChainSync. sync/src/lib.rs:1062 calls `executor.execute_block_parallel_at(..., &block.slash_evidence)`, which applies the identical slash to PI's storage — but ChainSync owns a separate `executor::Executor` and has no handle on DagConsensus, so PI's `validators_cache` is NEVER cleared. PI keeps the pre-slash 4-entry list for the rest of the process lifetime (or until it happens to build a block locally).

T3: The next anchor round R is decided on both nodes. dag.rs:1006 feeds the cached list into `engine.try_commit(..., &validators)`, and OrderingEngine::leader_for_round (consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs:910-930) hashes the ENTIRE list into the election seed:
    hasher.update(b"AINCORE_LEADER_V2"); hasher.update(round.to_le_bytes()); ... for (addr, stake) in validators { hasher.update(addr.as_bytes()); hasher.update(stake.to_le_bytes()); }
One removed member — or one stake differing by 1 — changes the seed AND the cumulative-stake walk, so NAS elects L_new and PI elects L_old for the SAME round R.

T4: `commit.leader` is used verbatim as BOTH the header proposer and the reward recipient (dag.rs:1039 `let reward_recipient = commit.leader.clone();`, then passed as `proposer_id` to `Block::new_with_roots_at` at dag.rs:1179 and as `proposer_hex` to `execute_block_parallel_at` at dag.rs:1113). `proposer_id` is folded into `calculate_header_hash` (consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:283). Result: two different header hashes at the same height, and — once fees are non-zero — two different state roots.

Secondary effect on the same call: dag.rs:1049 builds `stake_by_addr` from the same cached list; that map is the WEIGHT vector for `bft_block_timestamp`. A stale stake map moves the stake-weighted median onto a different vertex timestamp, changing `header.timestamp` by itself even when the leader happens to agree.

Tertiary effect: `direct_quorum_met` (ordering.rs:641) computes >2/3 against the stale `total_stake`, so the two nodes can disagree about whether round R is committable at all — that shifts the height<->anchor mapping, which is the exact class of bug B4b was meant to close.

confirmed.title: Block-carried slash_evidence is collected from per-node gossip state while EVERY validator builds EVERY block, so evidence_root (and the slash writes behind state_root) differ for identical committed content
confirmed.header_field_or_state: header.evidence_root (folded into calculate_header_hash), header.state_root (jail marker + stake burn written by apply_slash_evidence)
confirmed.divergence_sequence:
The evidence-carrying design is only safe when ONE proposer builds each block. Here the opposite is documented as the design: consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:52-54 says "EVERY validator deterministically builds EVERY block, so the signer is the node that built this copy". Every builder therefore stamps its OWN local view into the header.

T0: Validator X equivocates at round R (or, symmetrically, an equivocation proof is gossiped). dag.rs:1677 (`apply_equivocation_slash`, local detection) and dag.rs:1795 (`handle_equivocation_proof`, inbound gossip) both latch `sys:equiv_seen:{offender}:{round}`. Whether a given node holds that key is a pure function of which gossip messages that node received — it is not derived from the committed vertex sequence.

T1: NAS received the proof; PI did not (a dropped gossip message, or PI was mid-catch-up and the re-gossip landed before it was listening).

T2: Both nodes commit the same anchor and reach dag.rs:1110:
    let slash_evidence = executor.collect_slash_evidence();
core/executor/src/lib.rs:2178 scans NAS's local store and finds the equivocation row, so NAS gets `slash_evidence = [ {"kind":"equivocation", ...} ]`. PI's scan is empty, so PI gets `[]`.

T3: dag.rs:1113 passes the evidence into `execute_block_parallel_at`, which calls `apply_slash_evidence` (core/executor/src/lib.rs:1926 -> 2289). NAS writes `validator:jailed:{X}`, the slash tombstone, and the pruned `sys:validators` / `sys:validator_set:v1` — all through `logged_put`, so all of them land in `block_write_log` and are folded into the state root at core/executor/src/lib.rs:1939-1963. PI writes nothing, and (per the empty-writes guard at 1946) leaves its root untouched.

T4: dag.rs:1191 passes the same `slash_evidence` vector into `Block::new_with_roots_at`, which computes `evidence_root = calculate_evidence_root(&slash_evidence)` (consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:226) and folds it into the header hash (consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:285-287). NAS's block at height H has a non-empty evidence_root and state_root S1; PI's block at H has an empty evidence_root and state_root S0.

Result: two byte-different blocks at the same height from the same committed vertex sequence. Neither can adopt the other — sync/src/lib.rs:1097 fires SYNC_HEIGHT_ALREADY_EXECUTED and drops the peer's batch, and `verify_execution_roots` would reject it anyway.

The same divergence is reachable with no Byzantine validator at all through the downtime branch (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2195): the `atts` array embedded in the evidence item is literally the set of attestation JSONs THIS node happened to receive, so two nodes that both reach the >2/3 reporter quorum still serialize different arrays and therefore different evidence_root values.

confirmed.title: leader_for_round is a pure function of a validator set read from a cache that is invalidated ONLY on the local block-build path — a node whose blocks arrive via ChainSync elects anchor leaders from a pre-slash validator set forever
confirmed.header_field_or_state: header.proposer_id (reward_recipient = commit.leader), header.state_root (fee/reward recipient), and the anchor commit/skip decision itself (leader_vertex_hash / direct_quorum_met)
confirmed.divergence_sequence:
1. Cluster runs with 4 validators in `sys:validators`. Every node's `validators_cache` is populated once (dag.rs:2326) and thereafter returned from the cache (dag.rs:2321-2324).
2. PI falls behind (gossip hole / the stall above). NAS's executor jails PI for downtime and rewrites the active set: core/executor/src/lib.rs:2489 `let _ = self.logged_put("sys:validators", &new_json);` after `vals.retain(|(_, w)| *w > 0)` — the set goes 4 -> 3.
3. NAS took that path through its LOCAL block build, so it reaches dag.rs:1250 `self.invalidate_validators_cache();` and its next `get_validator_set_with_stake()` returns the 3-validator set.
4. PI receives the SAME block through ChainSync. The sync import executes it, applies the same slash evidence, and writes the same 3-entry `sys:validators` to PI's RocksDB — but the sync path never touches DagConsensus, and `invalidate_validators_cache` has exactly ONE non-test caller in the whole repo (dag.rs:1250, inside the local-build loop). PI's in-memory cache still holds 4 entries.
5. `leader_for_round` hashes the WHOLE set into its seed: `hasher.update(b"AINCORE_LEADER_V2"); hasher.update(round.to_le_bytes()); ... for (addr, stake) in validators { hasher.update(addr.as_bytes()); hasher.update(stake.to_le_bytes()); }`. Adding/removing one entry changes the seed for EVERY round, and the stake-weighted cumulative walk runs over a different total_stake. So from that moment PI elects a different leader for essentially every anchor round.
6. Consequences, all divergent: (a) `leader_vertex_hash(r, ...)` looks for a different author's vertex, so PI's `direct_quorum_met` and its ancestry SKIP proof decide DIFFERENT anchor rounds -> a different anchor->height mapping; (b) even where the anchor round agrees, `reward_recipient = commit.leader` becomes PI's stale-set leader, which is written straight into the header as proposer_id and is bound into calculate_header_hash; (c) the same recipient is passed to `execute_block_parallel_at(..., &reward_recipient, ...)`, so the fee/reward sweep lands on a different account -> different state_root.
7. Two honest nodes, identical committed vertex sequence, different proposer_id and different state_root at the same height.
Note the cache is also never invalidated on epoch advance or on any state change applied purely through the sync path, so this is not limited to slashing.

The `if reason == "downtime"` block runs only after verify_slash_evidence returns Ok for a block-carried item whose attestations each carry `reporter_pubkey` + `signature` and pass Ed25519 verification with >2/3 reporter stake (executor:2260-2261, 2272-2279). The sole producer of downtime items is collect_slash_evidence (called at dag.rs:1112), which skips every persisted attestation lacking a signature — executor:2198 `if a.get("signature").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).is_none() { continue; }`. And no production writer ever persists a signature: handle_remote_attestation verifies the gossip signature then stores a REBUILT payload containing only offender/epoch/reporter/round/rounds_missed (dag.rs:2077-2083), and the self-observation writer stores the same unsigned shape (dag.rs:661-667); signature/reporter_pubkey are added only on the wire (dag.rs:1544-1546). grep for reporter_pubkey shows signed attestation JSON only in tests (consensus/consensus/src/tests.rs, core/node/tests/h02_libp2p_gossip.rs, core/executor/src/lib.rs:5054). Therefore `groups` in collect_slash_evidence is always empty, no block ever carries a verifying kind:"downtime" item, line 2296 never executes, and it cannot explain the zero-tx PI/NAS fork. Residual note (not the reported divergence, not honest-node reachable): a Byzantine proposer retaining wire-level signatures could craft a verifying downtime item, after which this scan WOULD diverge — so replacing the local scan_prefix with deletion of the exact reporter keys named in the verified item is still worth doing defensively.

refuted.title: Governance execution at the epoch boundary writes consensus-visible state (economic params, @0x1 module bytecode, stdlib version) with raw db.put, bypassing the state-root write log, and gates a module install on an operator-staged key nothing in the repo writes
refuted.header_field_or_state: header.state_root of every LATER block (via burn_percentage read at executor:1838 and via the Move stdlib bytecode the VM resolves for advance_epoch/distribute_rewards)
refuted.divergence_sequence: drive_governance runs inside the epoch boundary on BOTH the build and sync paths (core/executor/src/lib.rs:1256, called from maybe_advance_epoch), so it executes on zero-transaction blocks too. Every write it makes uses raw `self.db.put(...)`, never logged_put, so NONE of it enters block_effective_writes and NONE of it is covered by the block's state_root: update_economic_config -> `sys:config:base_reward` / `sys:config:halving_interval` / `sys:config:burn_percentage` (common/storage/src/lib.rs:702-718), set_federation_key -> `sys:config:federation_addr` (storage:667), apply_module_upgrade -> `module_0x1_{name}` (gov:614) and `sys:stdlib_version` (gov:622), plus save_proposal's put_object. Two consequences. (a) Root blindness: the boundary block's state_root is byte-identical on two nodes whose economic params or stdlib bytecode now differ, so the divergence is invisible at the block where it happens and only surfaces one or many blocks later. (b) A real split: `apply_module_upgrade` reads its bytecode from `sys:pending_module_upgrade:{name}` (gov:551), and grep across the workspace finds NO production writer for that prefix — it is staged out-of-band, per machine. Interleaving: proposal P (UpgradeModule staking) passes and queues. At boundary height H, NAS has the staged bytecode, so `apply_module_upgrade` installs new `module_0x1_staking` and bumps `sys:stdlib_version`; PI has nothing staged, so line 551's ok_or fires, execute_proposal_at returns Err, the driver logs 'execute failed' (gov:764) and P stays Queued. Because none of those writes are logged, block H's state_root matches on both nodes — no alarm. At the next boundary H+I, maybe_advance_epoch calls `0x1::epoch::advance_epoch` (executor:1224), which drives staking emission through the now-DIFFERENT staking bytecode on NAS: different vm_changes, different logged writes, different state_root at H+I with zero transactions in either block. The same shape holds for burn_percentage: executor:1838 `let burn_pct = self.db.get_burn_percentage() as u128;` reads `sys:config:burn_percentage` inside execution, a value only ever set by this unlogged governance path.

votes.reason: Path is dead in production and the claimed asymmetry is operator-supplied, not honest-node interleaving. (1) drive_governance (core/executor/src/lib.rs:1339-1346) calls process_due_proposals, which walks the Rust active index; the ONLY writer of that index is save_proposal->maintain_active_index (governance/governance/src/lib.rs:658), whose production callers do not exist: aincore_createProposal and aincore_vote are explicitly DISABLED at core/node/src/api_local.rs:1160-1181 ("submit a signed transaction calling 0x1::governance::create_proposal via aincore_sendTransaction"), GovernanceManager::create_proposal is called only from tests, and test_seed_proposal is #[doc(hidden)] "Test-only helper" (lib.rs:783-787). Real governance runs inside the Move module 0x1::governance (escrow/fee-burn resources at executor:2765,2769; genesis GovernanceState at core/node/src/genesis.rs:576), i.e. through logged VM changes. So load_active_index returns empty on every node at every boundary: no update_economic_config, no apply_module_upgrade, no unlogged write executes. (2) The UpgradeModule split needs sys:pending_module_upgrade:{name} staged on one machine only; grep confirms the only writers are inside governance/src/lib.rs mod tests (1226-1475), so on real nodes lib.rs:551-560's ok_or_else fires identically everywhere -> deterministic Err on all nodes. Requiring an operator to hand-write a RocksDB key on one node is differing inputs, not two honest nodes on the same committed sequence. (3) The burn_percentage channel cannot alter a zero-tx block: executor:1838-1842 computes burnt_fees = total_fees * pct / 100 = 0 and reward_amount = 0 when total_fees = 0, and the guarded blocks `if burnt_fees > 0` (:1847) and `if reward_amount > 0` (:1878) never run. (4) Consequence (a), root blindness, is not divergence: an unlogged write with an identical value on every node leaves every root identical. Residual (not the reported finding): if the Rust GovernanceManager path is ever re-enabled, update_economic_config (common/storage/src/lib.rs:702-718) and apply_module_upgrade (governance/src/lib.rs:613-623) would sit outside the state root and should be hardened — but that is latent, not a live divergence source, and cannot explain the fork at height 5077.

The cited unlogged writes are real (governance/governance/src/lib.rs:613-623 uses raw db.put, and drive_governance at core/executor/src/lib.rs:1339-1346 holds only the bare Arc<StateDB>), but the divergence chain is unreachable in production. process_due_proposals (governance/governance/src/lib.rs:732-783) iterates load_active_index (:668-674), which returns Ok(Vec::new()) unless gov:active_proposal_ids exists. That key is written only by store_active_index <- maintain_active_index <- save_proposal (:646-658), whose only callers are create_proposal (:344), vote (:415,:453), tally_at/execute_proposal_at (:527) and test_seed_proposal (:789) - none of which has a non-test caller anywhere in the workspace. The two mutating RPCs are hard-disabled with code -32040 (core/node/src/api_local.rs:1160-1168 and 1177-1183) and aincore_tally is explicitly read-only (api_local.rs:1198-1207). Move-side 0x1::governance::create_proposal writes resource_ keys, while get_proposal (:793-803) reads db.get_object filtered on type_struct == "0x1::governance::Proposal" (the object store) - no bridge exists. So the index is empty on every node, drive_governance is a no-op at every boundary, and apply_module_upgrade (:538) never runs; the missing sys:pending_module_upgrade writer is moot. The burn_percentage limb dies the same way: sys:config:burn_percentage is written only by StateDB::update_economic_config (common/storage/src/lib.rs:702-718), which has zero callers, so executor:1838 reads the same genesis value on all nodes (and with zero txs total_fees=0, so burnt_fees=0 regardless). Finally the proposed trigger is not an honest-node interleaving at all - it requires an operator to hand-stage bytecode into exactly one machine's RocksDB, i.e. differing inputs - and cannot explain the observed zero-transaction fork since no proposal object can exist. The remaining "root blindness" observation is conceded by the finding to produce byte-identical roots, so it is a detection gap, not a divergence cause; note also that the epoch-advance writes it lumps in DO enter the root via commit_kv_updates -> log_block_write (core/executor/src/lib.rs:1090-1096), and rotate_validator_epoch's raw puts are documented consensus metadata (executor:1259-1266).
